claims.text: SummIt achieves a G-Eval quality score of 4.33 on CNN/DM under zero-shot settings compared to 3.46 for standard ChatGPT.
SummIt achieves a FactCC score of 36.00 and DAE score of 33.02 on XSum compared to FactCC 28.00 and DAE 10.34 for standard ChatGPT.
Integrating OpenIE knowledge extraction into SummIt increases the summary DAE score on XSum to 90.36.
Approximately 90% of summary revisions executed by the LLM summarizer adhere to feedback provided by the LLM evaluator.
The proportion of human-judged beneficial summary refinements drops to 50-60% after two or more iterations.
In human preference evaluations, SummIt summaries achieve a 0.52 preference rating on CNN/DM and 0.38 on XSum, outperforming standard ChatGPT.

evidence.description: Table 2 shows G-Eval scores for CNN/DM in zero-shot setting: ChatGPT is 3.46 and SummIt is 4.33.
Table 4 reports FactCC and DAE metrics on XSum: ChatGPT achieves 28.00 FactCC and 10.34 DAE, while SummIt achieves 36.00 FactCC and 33.02 DAE.
Table 4 demonstrates SummIt-IE achieves DAE score of 90.36 compared to SummIt baseline's 33.02.
Figure 3 bottom plot shows that approximately 90% of edits made by the summarizer align with evaluator feedback across iterations.
Figure 3 top plot shows the ratio of edits improving the summary falls to around 50-60% after 2 or more iterations.
Table 3 reports Human Preference test results: SummIt achieves 0.52 on CNN/DM and 0.38 on XSum vs ChatGPT's 0.34 and 0.24.

methodologies.name: SummIt Iterative Refinement Framework
methodologies.description: A framework that uses separate LLMs as summarizer and evaluator to iteratively generate, evaluate, and edit summaries via pre-defined operation feedback (Add, Remove, Rephrase, Simplify, Keep).

methodologies.name: SummIt with Knowledge Extractor (SummIt-IE)
methodologies.description: An extension of SummIt incorporating OpenIE to extract knowledge triplets from the source document to guide faithfulness in both summary refinement and self-evaluation.

methodologies.name: SummIt with Topic Extractor (SummIt-Topic)
methodologies.description: An extension of SummIt for aspect-focused summarization that extracts topic-relevant snippets from source documents to control the focus of generated summaries based on user queries.

limitations.text: One-shot end-to-end summarization systems frequently suffer from hallucinations and lack controllability.
Standard evaluation metrics like ROUGE rely on imperfect reference summaries and do not accurately reflect LLM summary quality.

The framework suffers from an over-correction issue where the LLM evaluator continuously requests revisions based on its internal evaluation criteria rather than human judgment criteria as iteration count increases.
Evaluation was limited to a sampled subset of 1000 test examples per dataset due to API budget constraints.
Experiments were instantiated solely using OpenAI's gpt-3.5-turbo model, without testing across diverse open-source or closed LLM backbones.

future_work.text: Develop better stopping criteria and integrate human-in-the-loop feedback to mitigate the over-correction problem in iterative summarization systems.
